segments.label: 背景
segments.text: In a campus library, our class tested an AI assistant that suggests articles for design projects.
segments.meaningBasis: 场景与主题：校园图书馆里全班测试一个为设计项目推荐文章的 AI 助手。

segments.label: 最初有用
segments.text: At first, the suggestions looked useful because the assistant found papers on the topics we entered.
segments.meaningBasis: 最初印象的依据：按输入话题找到了论文，所以『看起来』有用。

segments.label: 发现问题
segments.text: But when we checked the sources, several summaries missed important limits in the original papers.
segments.meaningBasis: but 转折的对象：核查来源后发现，若干摘要漏掉了原论文的重要限制。

segments.label: 最终结论
segments.text: So our conclusion was narrower than we expected: the tool can help us find papers worth reading, but we still need to read each source before using it to support a design decision.
segments.meaningBasis: 最终评价（带限定）：能帮助找到值得读的论文；但支撑设计决策前必须自己读每篇来源——不是『不能用』也不是『随便用』。

scripts.speakerLabel: synthetic-A（Zira，与 D2 同声源不同稿——18 §5 要求 L2 与 D2 不同情境）

segments.label: 做了什么
segments.text: We made a map that tells visitors which rooms in the museum are busy.
segments.meaningBasis: 项目内容：一张告诉游客哪些展厅拥挤的地图。

segments.label: 预期
segments.text: We expected people to choose a quieter route.
segments.meaningBasis: 团队预期：人们会因此选更安静的路线。

segments.label: 实际观察
segments.text: In fact, some visitors walked toward the crowded rooms because they thought something interesting was happening there.
segments.meaningBasis: 实际行为与机制：有人反而走向拥挤展厅——因为他们以为那里有有意思的事。because 解释的是游客的动机。

segments.label: 判定
segments.text: The map was working as designed, but our assumption about what visitors wanted was incomplete.
segments.meaningBasis: but 对照的两件事：地图按设计正常工作 ↔ 团队对游客需求的假设不完整。失灵的是假设，不是地图。

segments.label: 下一步
segments.text: Next month, we will ask visitors why they chose a route before we change the design.
segments.meaningBasis: 后续计划：先问游客选路线的原因，再决定改不改设计。

scripts.speakerLabel: synthetic-A（Zira，单一英文声源——换真人间隙如实标注；与 D2/L2 不同情境）

segments.label: 做了什么
segments.text: In our study group, we set up daily review reminders in October. The idea was to send a short message every evening at eight.
segments.meaningBasis: 项目内容：十月起设了每天晚上八点的复习提醒。

segments.label: 预期
segments.text: We expected the daily reminders to help everyone keep up with the readings.
segments.meaningBasis: 团队预期：每天提醒能帮大家跟上阅读。

segments.label: 实际观察
segments.text: In fact, after two weeks, most of us ignored the evening messages, and the reminders stopped feeling useful.
segments.meaningBasis: 实际结果：两周后大多数人忽略了晚间消息——提醒不再有用。in fact 分开预期与实际。

segments.label: 结论与限制
segments.text: So here is our conclusion: reminders do help, but only before exam week, when everyone wants a schedule; on normal weeks, we will turn them off and review on our own.
segments.meaningBasis: 最终主张带限制：提醒有用——但只在考试周前（大家想要时间表时）；平时周关掉、自己安排。限制是使用条件，不是“提醒没用”。

scripts.speakerLabel: synthetic-A（Zira，单一英文声源——换材料换情境，“换声音”待真人录音，如实开放）

segments.label: 做了什么
segments.text: Our dorm floor shares one washing machine, so we made a sign-up sheet for laundry times.
segments.meaningBasis: 背景与做法：全层共用一台洗衣机，做了洗衣时间登记表。

segments.label: 为何这么做
segments.text: Before the sheet, two or three people always picked the same hour and argued about it.
segments.meaningBasis: 动因：表做出来之前总有人撞点吵架——表是为了解决真实冲突。

segments.label: 何时有效
segments.text: The sheet works well on weekdays, because everyone is in class at different hours.
segments.meaningBasis: 主张成立范围：工作日好用——大家上课时间错开。

segments.label: 限制与决定
segments.text: But on Friday evenings everyone wants to wash at the same time, so the sheet does not help then. We will keep it for weekdays only.
segments.meaningBasis: 限制说得很具体：周五晚上大家同时想洗，表帮不上忙——决定是只在工作日保留。限制是适用范围，不是“表没用”。
